question: Which of the following are the cellular structures responsible for protein synthesis?
solution:
The correct answer is** ​__Ribosomes__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Protein synthesis is the primary function of ''**ribosomes**''
 
• Ribosomes are the site for ''**protein synthesis**'' so they are also called the ''protein factory'' of the cell.
 
• There are two types of ribosomes
 
 
• **Eukaryotic ribosomes** - 80s - occur in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cell
 
• **Prokaryotic ribosomes** - 70s - occur in the cytoplasm as well as are associated with the cell membrane of prokaryotic cell
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Mitochondria

 
 
 
Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles that are the main sites of Oxygenic respiration. This process results in the formation of the energy currency of the cell, call as ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate).

 
 
 

 
 
Chloroplast

 
 
 
Chloroplast is double-membrane bound organelles that are the main sites of photosynthesis in plants resulting in the production of Glucose by assimilation of CO2 and H2O.

 
 
 

 
 
Lysosomes

 
 
 
Lysosomes are suicide bags that contain hydrolytic enzymes.
